acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Giants family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Primordial Titan, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Marching-Valley Worldboss (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A walking mountain range with an inhabited valley across the back, glaciers in the beard, cloud banks at the waist, warm furnace-mouth eyes, and four colossal rune anchors integrated into distinct forests, slopes, standing stones, and watersheds.

Signature mechanic: March of the Range: the battle occupies the valley on the Titan's back. At four gait beats, the Titan repeats the family grammar at landscape scale: a forested ridge falls like Timber Fall, a glacier rolls loose like Hill Roll, a chain of standing stones sweeps around a central peak like Megalith Orbit, and shoulder rivers reroute through Three Watersheds. A Brute, Hill Giant, Stone Giant, or Mountain Lord operates the matching rune anchor; disabling that crew and breaking its anchor removes the phase. After two anchors fall, the Titan kneels and rotates the valley ninety degrees, opening new paths through its beard glaciers rather than becoming a larger version of the Champion.
battlefieldDuty: Serve as the changing arena itself, carrying a valley that tilts through timber, slope, orbit, and watershed phases while lower Giants operate visible anchors across its back.
constructionDimensions: Body geology becomes volcanic but remains load-bearing: clinker shelves, basalt plates, charred pine roots, obsidian chain guards, and cooled lava crust form over recognizable hide and stone growth.
Motion and surface behavior expose heat cycling through opening crust vents, directional ash falls, steam where runoff crosses hot seams, and dark cooling plates that contract between attacks.
counterplay: Use the announced landscape route to reach the active lower Giant, defeat or displace it, fracture the exposed rune anchor during the Titan's footfall recovery, and relocate to a surviving standing-stone shelter before the valley rotates; every destroyed anchor permanently removes one gait phase. Affinity signal: A basalt joint opens to a bright heat sink after committed movement; striking the cooling seam or redirecting shoulder runoff into it fractures the loaded plate.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only fire treatment without volcanic materials, vent cycles, and heat-driven surface change
Glow-only fire treatment without load-bearing crust or exposed cooling seams
Featureless flame bodies that erase humanoid anatomy and lived-in geology
Uniform lava coating that hides chain pivots, heels, and rune anchors
identityInvariants: Humanlike proportions scaled upward with a heavy brow, thick limbs, dense bone, and a slight stoop that communicates the body's own weight.
Stone grey, granite blue-grey, earth brown, moss green, glacier white, and warm amber eyes remain the family palette without requiring an elemental origin.
Rough hide, raw stone, moss, lichen, pine, iron chain, and rope accumulate as bodily geology and oversized practical tools.
Chains, standing-stone jewelry, skin runes, and whole trees function as ornament at a scale that stays legible from the arena.
Raw scale and geological coverage escalate together until the Sovereign carries a valley, but every form retains recognizable humanoid load paths and slow committed motion.
telegraph: Clouds shear at the waist, furnace-warm eyes narrow without casting an aura, one valley rune darkens, and the corresponding forest, glacier, standing-stone chain, or river system begins moving several beats before the Titan's foot lands.
